facts.statement: Tamarro is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur named after a local mythological creature.
facts.quote: Tamarro (named after a mythological creature in local culture) is a genus of troodontid theropod from the Late Cretaceous Talarn Formation (Tremp Group) of Spain.

facts.statement: The only known species, Tamarro insperatus, is represented by a partial metatarsal fossil described in 2021.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Tamarro insperatus, known from a partial metatarsal described in 2021.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, a metatarsal found in 2003 at the Sant Romà d'Abella site, belongs to the Talarn Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype of Tamarro, MCD-7073, a metatarsal, was found in 2003 at the Sant Romà d'Abella site, belonging to the Talarn Formation of the Tremp Group.

facts.statement: Sellés and colleagues formally described the genus and species Tamarro insperatus in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, Sellés et al. described it as a new genus and species, Tamarro insperatus

facts.statement: The specific name insperatus means "unexpected" because the fossil was an unexpected find.
facts.quote: the specific name means "unexpected", referring to the unexpected discovery of the fossil.

facts.statement: Tamarro is classified in the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae, representing the first European member of this group.
facts.quote: Sellés et al. placed Tamarro in the Jinfengopteryginae, making it the first member of the subfamily from Europe.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Tamarro's ancestors migrated from Asia to Europe between the Cenomanian and Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: They also suggested that its ancestors migrated from Asia to Europe sometime between the Cenomanian and the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Analysis indicates the holotype was a subadult that experienced rapid early growth.
facts.quote: Analysis of the holotype suggests it was a subadult; its large size suggests it grew quickly early in its life.

facts.statement: Tamarro lived on the Ibero-Armorican Island during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Tamarro lived on the Ibero-Armorican Island, and its discovery increases knowledge about the diversity of small theropods on the Cretaceous European archipelago.

facts.statement: Tamarro coexisted with dwarf sauropods and lambeosaurine hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: It would have lived at the same time as dwarf sauropods and lambeosaurine hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Tamarro lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
